pill.desc: sterile injection in single-dose and multiple-dose vials

clues.kinetics: Completely and rapidly absorbed after intramuscular injection, and about 91% bound to plasma proteins. It is conjugated in the liver, and its inactive conjugate is eliminated mainly by the kidneys.
clues.substance: Molecular weight 321.16. It is a powder that is almost insoluble in water.
clues.product: An NDA product as injection in 2 mg/mL and 4 mg/mL strengths, in single-dose and multiple-dose vials.
clues.safety: Boxed warning on concomitant opioid use, abuse and dependence. Contraindicated in acute narrow-angle glaucoma and sleep apnea syndrome; somnolence and hypotension are common.
clues.indication: Treatment of status epilepticus, and preanesthetic use in adults for sedation, relief of anxiety and reduced recall of the day of surgery.
clues.mechanism: It has antianxiety, sedative and anticonvulsant effects; the label gives no molecular mechanism.

tell: Only 0.3% of a dose is excreted unchanged; it is glucuronidated rather than oxidized, so liver disease barely alters clearance.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: INTRAVENOUS INJECTION For the treatment of status epilepticus, the usual recommended dose of ATIVAN Injection is 4 mg given slowly (2 mg/min)
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: the terminal half-life and total clearance averaged 14±5 hours
